NEWCASTLE, England, Nov 21 : Arsenal missed the chance to go eight points clear at the top of the Premier League as they were held to a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Saturday, with Mikel Arteta's side having to fight back from 2-1 down after a spirited display from their hosts. Arsenal looked set for an easy evening in the first half and they took the lead in the 33rd minute, Eberechi Eze latching on to a superb angled pass from Kai Havertz to sweep the ball into the net. Booed off at the break, Newcastle levelled four minutes into the second half as Martin Odegaard was robbed from a throw-in by William Osula. The Danish striker fed the ball to Harvey Barnes, who took a touch before rifling the ball past the keeper. In the 62nd minute the home side went ahead, Malick Thiaw bundling the ball into the net from close range after Arsenal failed to clear a corner. Arsenal keeper David Raya then suffered an arm injury and was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Nov 21 : Rassie Erasmus’ watch-along in South Africa’s 20-17 loss to Ireland on Saturday provided a range of emotions but not much in the way of insight from the Springbok coach, who is serving a six-match ban for criticising match officials. Erasmus hosted a live-stream of himself watching the game from the team’s Dublin hotel, and in the week had over 100,000 people request to view the match with him on a platform he had created. He was sat in what appeared to be a conference room, drinking diet coke and getting increasingly animated as the game went on. Erasmus celebrated his team’s two tries as you would expect him too, but largely sat sullen without much in the way of expression.

NICE, France, Nov 21 : Champions Paris St Germain fought back after conceding early at Nice on Saturday to win 3-2 and extend their Ligue 1 lead to five points, but it came at a potentially heavy cost. France international Desire Doue injured his knee not long after he had put PSG 2-1 ahead and left the pitch in tears. "We need to wait for tomorrow's medical examinations, but it is clearly a serious injury. We could see that on television,” PSG coach Luis Enrique said. "I have spoken with him; he is in the dressing room. We need to wait for the final medical examinations to know exactly what the injury is, but it is clearly a serious one."

DUBLIN, Nov 21 : Two first-half tries from Rob Baloucoune helped a rejuvenated Ireland beat South Africa 20-17 on Saturday but a losing bonus point was enough to book the world champions a place in next weekend's Nations Championship final. With Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus watching on from his hotel serving the first of a six-match ban, Ireland dominated the first period and led the subdued Springboks 17-10 at halftime thanks to Baloucoune's tries and one from Ronan Kelleher. A Sam Prendergast penalty stretched the lead to 10 points and while a Malcolm Marx try cut it to three just before the hour, the Springboks could not breach the excellent Irish defence and fell to back-to-back defeats. "It's some effort from the lads. It's never going to be perfect against the world's best but we kept getting back into the game when we've just had something that's disappointing," said Ireland coach Andy Farrell.

"It's just shows the character of the lads. It shows us where we're at 10 months out from a World Cup." Farrell's men, who began the day with an outside shot of topping the Northern Hemisphere standings, cannot catch England but are guaranteed a top-three finish and one of the marquee games at the November 27-29 finals weekend at Twickenham. ERASMUS WATCHES ON FROM AFAR The build-up was dominated by Erasmus' ban for questioning the integrity of match officials following last week's loss to France and while some visiting fans sported masks of their suspended coach, his players' performance offered little support. They had demolished the Ireland scrum when they won in Dublin a year ago and looked ready to pick up where they left off on Saturday with a couple of early easy shoves handing Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu the opportunity to put them 3-0 up. But Ireland were a different beast this time and roared straight back, stretching the visitors with Stuart McCloskey finding Baloucoune with a fine long pass for the winger to step smartly inside for the opening try of the game on eight minutes. The in-form Ulster man was almost in again shortly after, only to lose his grip on the ball at the last second but he only had to wait a couple more minutes to notch his fourth try of the competition. While a rare obliteration of the South Africa scrum brought the biggest roar of the game and celebrations among the Irish pack who competed far better throughout, it was the Springboks' steamrolling set-piece that set up Morne van den Berg to level the scores against the run of play four minutes from the break. However, the hosts took a deserved lead into the break when Kelleher, starting at hooker with captain Dan Sheehan playing at number eight for the first time, powered over from a smart lineout maul five yards out from the Springbok line.  South Africa started the second half a little better and Canan Moodie, an early replacement for the injured Damian Willemse, was a stray boot from a brilliant finish in the corner. But they could not get any kind of flow into their game, even after the deployment of their 'Bomb Squad' from the bench helped lead to the converted Marx try that set up the tight finish. Ireland crucially remained on the front foot and stood up to some late pressure to the dismay of Erasmus, who smashed the table at full time and shouted at a TV during a live online watch party he was hosting four kilometres away at the team hotel. "We never promise we're going to win every game, but we know as a group that we can definitely be better," said South Africa captain Siya Kolisi. "I don't question the boys' effort, I don't question their mindset and wanting to win all the time but it's just finding plans to be better and executing better... There's a lot that we know that we need to fix, but we do know how to fix it."

Nov 21 : World chess governing body FIDE referred Magnus Carlsen to its Ethics and Disciplinary Commission (EDC) after the Norwegian forfeited three games during a pilot event for the Total Chess World Championship Tour in Budapest, the federation said on Saturday. In a statement, FIDE criticised Carlsen for missing three scheduled games against Vladislav Artemiev while their 17th-place playoff was still undecided. Carlsen forfeited both rapid games on the opening day of the match and a fast classic game on day two before prevailing in an armageddon tie-break. “Given GM Carlsen’s stature and his significant role in promoting chess, such actions are particularly concerning, as they may damage the reputation of competitions and demonstrate a lack of respect for opponents, spectators, and tournament partners,” FIDE said.

LONDON, Nov 21 : Xabi Alonso's Chelsea players looked brittle, unsure and devoid of ideas as they were crushed 4-1 by visitors Leeds United in the Premier League on Saturday. A first win at Stamford Bridge for the Yorkshire side since 1999 lifted them into sixth place in the table as Chelsea, who have now lost three games in a row, tumbled from fifth to eighth. It was also the second straight home defeat for the Blues who were outgunned 2-0 before the international break by fierce London rivals Tottenham Hotspur, then succumbed to a colourless 1-0 defeat at Sunderland. Leeds more than deserved their comprehensive victory. Although Chelsea went ahead through a powerful 25th-minute finish from Emmanuel Emegha, making his first start for Chelsea, it was against the run of play.

"Today I felt we were in a fragile moment mentally," Alonso told reporters. "It went wrong after the equaliser. We lost completely the momentum," the former Spain international added. "From that moment they start believing and we start not believing." Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored from the spot in the 53rd minute after a long VAR check backed referee Michael Oliver in giving a handball decision against Morgan Rogers. Okafor, completely unmarked, hooked the ball into Martinez's net in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson scored in added time. It had started as an untidy game full of niggly fouls but with none of the violence of the infamously bad-temperered 20th century clashes between the sides, culminating in the 1970 FA Cup final won in a replay by Chelsea on a mud pitch and dubbed the most brutal game in English domestic football.It was Leeds who showed the greater hunger, motivation and positive aggression on Saturday, forcing Chelsea's fragile defence, who have now shipped 20 goals this season, on to the back foot. "We were from the first minute to the last the better side," Leeds manager Daniel Farke said. "We have shown the desire to work and the hunger to dig in." Calvert-Lewin missed a hatful of early chances and Leeds finished with 21 shots to Chelsea's 14. "We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It's right we can enjoy this performance," Leeds captain and former Chelsea midfielder Ethan Ampadu told BBC TV.

LONDON, Nov 21 : Tottenham Hotspur teenager Luca Williams-Barnett became the club's youngest Premier League scorer since Gareth Bale as he marked his first top-flight start with the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday. Williams-Barnett, who turned 18 last month, stabbed home Pedro Porro's cross in the 15th minute and helped set up his side's second for Dominic Solanke with a jinking run. It was only a fifth Tottenham appearance for the England junior international but the winger rewarded manager Roberto de Zerbi's faith. "Luca was magnificent today. We see him in training every day, we know what a player he is. He's such a talent, honestly," Solanke said.

The global players' union was responding to recent remarks by senior Bayern officials, including honorary president Uli Hoeness, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, about Musiala's future at the club. TURIN, Italy, Nov 21 : Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz battled back from a set down to beat American Ben Shelton 3-6 6-3 7-6(1) in their ATP Finals semi-final to charge into Sunday's showcase for the second consecutive year. Alcaraz, beaten by Shelton in the US Open quarter-finals on the Spaniard's return from a four-month injury break, stretched his winning run to 13 matches after back-to-back titles in Vienna and Paris. He will face either world number one Alexander Zverev or Daniil Medvedev of Russia, who meet later on Saturday. "I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning because I didn't start the match the way I wanted to," said Alcaraz, unbeaten on indoor courts this season.

"Just happy that I came back in the second set playing such great tennis, step by step, focused on all my things and ended up playing good tennis. The third set was even closer." Shelton, making his second consecutive appearance in the season finale, grabbed an early break to race to a 3-0 lead. Alcaraz, whose fitness had come under scrutiny after he left the court with heavy strapping on his left leg following Wednesday's win over Medvedev, had his thigh wrapped heavily against Shelton. He upped his game and started moving the American around more, engaging him in longer rallies. He earned two break points at 4-2 but could not convert either with Shelton's booming serve getting him out of trouble.  The world number four fired a second-serve ace on his first set point to move ahead but Alcaraz went 5-3 up in the second before serving out the second set. The pair traded blows in the third set before Alcaraz eased through the tiebreak, sealing the win with a return winner.

PORTIMAO, Portugal, Nov 21 : Marc Marquez's chance to clinch an eighth MotoGP title on Saturday ended in the gravel when the Ducati rider crashed out of third place on the penultimate lap of the Portuguese Grand Prix sprint which was won by Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi. Marquez had needed to outscore title rival Jorge Martin by just two points to be crowned champion on Saturday but the Ducati rider lost control on lap 11 as rain started to fall and he went out. Aprilia's Martin eventually finished fifth to reduce Marquez's lead to 55 points ahead of Sunday's race, where Marquez can still seal the title with a round to spare. "We have the big advantage (in points) luckily," Marquez said with a wry smile when speaking to TNT Sports.

"It was a very difficult sprint race, especially on that lap it started to rain more. When I arrived on that corner, I didn't realise that it was so wet. "It's true that the people want to celebrate as soon as possible but I'm calm. The good thing is that I'm perfect on the physical side, so tomorrow we will have another chance." Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez finished second while Gresini Racing's Alex Marquez completed the podium. The crash also keeps alive Bezzecchi's very slim title hopes but the Italian remains 62 points adrift and will need Marquez to score no further points this season to stay in contention. "I'm so happy. The sprint has been like a torture for me till now, so very, very happy to make this kind of result," said Bezzecchi after his first sprint victory of the season. "Huge thanks to the team because they never stop believing in me... Now we continue working for tomorrow and we will try our best also in the longer race (on Sunday)." MARQUEZ EXERCISES CAUTION Bezzecchi had broken the lap record to snatch pole and the Italian had the perfect start off the line while Fernandez found a way past a cautious Marquez to move up to second. Bezzecchi and Fernandez peeled away at the front and Marquez seemed to be holding up the rest of the pack while his brother Alex moved up to fourth behind him, with Martin back in seventh despite his best efforts to overtake riders. Martin continued to look for openings and although he moved up to sixth when he overtook VR46 Racing's Fabio di Giannantonio, he could not find a way past KTM's Pedro Acosta, who will be Marquez's teammate at Ducati next season. However, light rain had started to fall across the track and Marc crashed out right in front of his brother Alex, sliding into the gravel as shocked spectators looked on in disbelief. "Everything was going really under control... But then we arrive at turn seven and suddenly it was this slight rain that caused him to crash," Alex said. "Then for three to four corners I was super slow because I don't want to crash!" Alex then kept Acosta at bay on the last lap to secure the final podium spot, finishing less than half a second ahead of the KTM rider.

MANCHESTER, England, Nov 21 : Manchester City's slide from top of the table to a club in crisis reached an uncomfortable new low on Saturday when a 1-1 draw with Fulham extended a run that would have been virtually unthinkable only weeks ago. A team who opened the season with seven straight Premier League victories have now followed up with four successive games without a win.  The numbers are piling up. City have lost three of their last four league games, as many defeats as they suffered in their previous 36. They have also gone nine games across all competitions without a clean sheet. And beyond the statistics, it was the mood at the Etihad Stadium that told the full story.

As Fulham celebrated ending a run of 20 consecutive defeats against City and taking a point from the league giants for the first time in 15 years, thousands of home supporters headed for the exits before the final whistle.  Those who remained among the otherwise huge swathes of empty blue seats greeted the final whistle with a chorus of boos.  Glum-faced City boss Enzo Maresca trudged down the tunnel. "Tough moment in terms of results... we were anxious in terms of going behind," said Maresca, who had changed the pre-game routine by having the squad stay at the new hotel on the Etihad campus on Friday night. "In this moment all we can try to do is recover and we have another big game here on Tuesday (against Napoli in the Champions League).  "We changed a bit at halftime the way we were pressing. Second half we were much better. We had so many moments where we could have made a better choice but it's important that we arrived there and created chances and soon we can score more goals." Their next league game is a trip to league leaders Arsenal and suddenly it looks less like a title showdown than a test of City's nerve. The frustration stemmed as much from the performance as the result. City looked flat and passive for long stretches, vulnerable whenever Fulham attacked and strangely lacking urgency in possession.  During one stretch, exasperated supporters groaned when Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno was repeatedly allowed to take his time on the ball without any pressure. The intensity that has defined recent City sides was absent. Elliot Anderson's equaliser in the 57th minute at least rescued a point but the midfielder acknowledged that the recurring pattern of City falling behind was becoming a concern. "It's very frustrating," he said. "Going a goal down wasn't ideal but it seems to be happening. The second half was better, more intensity, we pushed higher. We just struggled to get the second goal. "We're working on that. We are doing everything we can to fix it." Anderson struck a volley into the bottom corner for his first league goal for City since joining from Nottingham Forest in the close season.  "That's my job on the edge of the box on corners from that side," he said. "Try to get a clean connection on target. Trying to stay calm in those situations and make good contact." The 24-year-old said there was no sense of panic despite a turbulent period for the club, with City's worsening form coinciding with their appeal against more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. City have denied any wrongdoing.
